newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Commercial Union sets date for Vietnam venture.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Union sets date for Vietnam venture.

text.p: Commercial Union plc (CU) said it would officially open a new joint venture insurance unit in Vietnam on November 18.
The deal makes CU the first foreign joint venture insurer to get the go-ahead from Vietnamese regulators, the company said in a statement.
CU's partners in the venture are Japan's Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd and Bao Viet, Vietnam's state-owned insurer.

The new venture, Vietnam International Assurance Company (VIA), has paid up share capital of US$6 million and is 51 percent owned by Bao Viet. Stakes of 24.5 percent each are contolled by the two foreign partners.
Plans for the venture were first revealed in January 1996.
John Davidson, CU manager for Asia based in Singapore, said the new company, Vietnam International Assurance Company (VIA), expected revenues of US$10 million over the next three years.

Premiums would be generated through support for Vietnam's US$22 billion Foreign Direct Ivestment programme which had 1,800 foreign projects pledged to date, much of which would otherwise be insured off-shore, the statement said.
"We see VIA contributing to the economic development of the country by supporting current developments and attracting new foreign investors," Davidson said.
